title: FromQuery
description: Learn how to bind query string parameters.

data.text: **[FromQuery]** binds action parameters from the query string. It is commonly used for filtering, sorting, and pagination because those values live naturally in the URL without requiring a request body.

Query string parameters are key-value pairs appended to the URL after the ? character. ASP.NET Core parses them, converts the values to the target parameter types, and applies default values when a parameter is absent.

terms.definition: An attribute that tells model binding to source a parameter from the query string.
The portion of a URL after the ? sign, containing key-value pairs separated by &.
A dedicated class that groups related query parameters so they can be bound as a single complex type.
A fallback value assigned to a parameter when the client omits it from the query string.

data.caption: How query string values are parsed and bound to action parameters.
data.definition:
flowchart TB
    A[/api/products?term=laptop&page=2&pageSize=20/] --> B{Parse Query String}
    B -->|term=laptop| C[Extract Values]
    B -->|page=2| C
    B -->|pageSize=20| C
    C --> D{Convert Types}
    D -->|Valid| E[Bind Parameter]
    D -->|Invalid| F[400 Bad Request]
    E --> G[Controller Action]
    F --> G

data.text: For simple filters, you can bind each query value to its own parameter. Use default values to make parameters optional.

data.title: Individual Query Parameters
data.content: Binding search and pagination values directly from the query string.

data.text: When you have many related options, create a dedicated query model class. ASP.NET Core binds each query key to a matching property by name.

data.title: Query Model Binding
data.content: Grouping query parameters into a single model class for cleaner signatures.

cards.title: Individual Parameters
cards.description: Bind each query value to a separate action parameter.
pros: Good for two or three values
cons: Method signature grows with each new option

cards.title: Query Model Class
cards.description: Group related options into a dedicated class and bind it once.
cons: Implicit binding can hide which values are expected

items.text: Use [FromQuery] for filtering, sorting, and pagination
Assign default values to optional parameters so clients can omit them
Validate ranges with [Range] when numeric parameters have upper or lower bounds
Use a query model class when the endpoint accepts more than three options
Limit maximum pageSize to prevent denial-of-service from huge result sets
Document expected query keys in OpenAPI so consumers know what to send

data.title: Build a Search Endpoint
data.description: Create a search action that supports filtering by category, sorting by price, and pagination.
steps: Create a ProductSearchParams class with properties: CategoryId (int?), SortBy (string), MinPrice (decimal?), MaxPrice (decimal?), Page (int), and PageSize (int).
Create a GET api/products/search action that accepts [FromQuery] ProductSearchParams.
Apply category and price filters when the corresponding values are present.
Sort by name ascending if SortBy is missing or unknown.
Return paginated results with metadata: page, pageSize, and totalCount.
data.expectedOutcome: A search endpoint that cleanly handles optional filters, validates input, and returns paginated product results.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: [FromQuery] binds values from the URL query string
Use it for filters, sorts, and pagination
Query model classes keep signatures clean and reusable
data.takeaway: FromQuery is the simplest way to accept optional input without a request body.
